feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong senior digital/public-sector CV with clear positioning, credible scope, and solid evidence of progression. It reads professionally and is largely error-free, but it is somewhat dense and repetitive, with a few style inconsistencies that reduce sharpness and impact.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear leadership narrative: strong progression at NACo culminating in director-level ownership of web, analytics, governance, and multimedia.  
- Good credibility signals: concrete scale markers like “10,000+ page website,” “3.5 million annual page views,” and “50+ internal publishers.”  
- Broad but relevant skill mix across strategy, platforms, analytics, content operations, and AI-enabled search.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce repetition and tighten structure: “digital strategy,” “governance,” “workflows,” and “communications operations” recur heavily across sections; consolidate Core Competencies/Topline Skills/Technical + IT.  
- Add more outcome-focused achievements: several bullets describe responsibilities rather than results; include measurable impact on engagement, efficiency, adoption, or campaign performance.  
- Fix stylistic inconsistencies: mixed punctuation and list formatting, inconsistent use of “and” vs “&,” and title casing such as “Coleman DAVIS” vs standard capitalization. Minor grammar/style edits: remove comma in “web, email, social, and multimedia” for consistency; “Ranked among the top public universities…” is weak/irrelevant in Education; “French (A2/Learning)” reads awkwardly—use “French (A2, learning).”
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible summary with clear seniority and public-sector focus. It reads well, but it overlaps heavily with the subtitle, core competencies, and work experience, so it would benefit from sharper differentiation and a few concrete signals of scale.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Tighten to one concise value proposition and add scale where possible, e.g. “10,000+ page platforms,” “3.5M annual page views,” or “50+ publishers.”
- Reduce list-like phrasing; group related capabilities into broader themes such as platform modernization, governance, and audience experience.
- Align style with the subtitle by emphasizing leadership scope and outcomes, not just functions performed.
- Suggested rewrite: Senior digital platform and communications leader with 12+ years of experience modernizing high-volume public-sector websites and content operations. Leads enterprise web strategy, governance, analytics, and editorial systems for mission-driven organizations, with experience scaling platforms serving millions of annual page views, supporting large publisher networks, and delivering AI-enabled search and multimedia experiences.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled user experiences” overlaps with core competencies and recent projects; consider narrowing to “AI-enabled search.”
- “Platforms, governance models and content operations” is echoed across multiple sections; avoid repeating all three here and elsewhere.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and work experience. It would be stronger if tightened into broader, less repetitive capability areas.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Consolidate overlapping items and sharpen wording: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance, editorial systems & publishing workflows • Analytics, reporting & optimization • Multi-channel communications leadership • AI-enabled search, automation & platform integration • Public-sector advocacy communications • Multimedia production, livestreaming & event operations
- Replace “operations” repetition with more varied terms like “leadership,” “workflows,” or “optimization.”
- Consider grouping related concepts to reduce list length and improve scanability.
- Keep the focus on strategic capabilities; leave tool-specific detail to Technical + IT.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise website modernization,” “analytics infrastructure,” “AI-enabled search,” and “multimedia production” are already emphasized in the header and Topline Skills.
- “Advocacy and public-sector communications” overlaps with both the header and multiple NACo roles.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshots, but the footer repeats achievements already covered in Work Experience and reads a bit dense. Tightening phrasing and emphasizing distinct outcomes or formats will make it feel more additive.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Add dates or “Selected recent projects” framing to reinforce recency and separate this from core experience.
- Tighten each item to one crisp line with parallel verbs and cleaner punctuation; spell out “10 x 20-foot” for consistency.
- Emphasize what is unique about each project: AI search UX, Drupal 10 microsite architecture, conference installation, or cross-channel video program.
- Consider this format: “AI Hybrid Search — Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience using hybrid retrieval, vector search, structured content workflows, and bill-level chat.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- AI Hybrid Search, microsite development, and advocacy video series closely overlap with bullets in the current and NACo roles.
- “Built/developed” repeats across all entries; vary verbs to avoid monotony.

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant current role, but it reads as a task list and overlaps heavily with the header, competencies, and NACo entries. Make it sharper by emphasizing this is a current strategic/technical consulting engagement and by tying bullets to concrete deliverables or outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Open with scope + client type + value: “Advise a U.S. national membership organization on digital strategy, Drupal platform improvements, and communications operations for enterprise web and campaign initiatives.”
- Tighten and combine overlapping bullets: merge “digital systems, workflows and analytics” with “governance, usability and operational best practices” into one outcome-oriented bullet.
- Rephrase for impact: “Built Drupal campaign microsites, modular storytelling components, and downloadable member toolkits” and “Delivered front-end/CMS enhancements and troubleshooting for high-traffic public web properties.”
- Add measurable outcomes where possible: number of sites/pages, users, publishers, campaign launches, toolkit downloads, search accuracy gains, reduced publishing time, or improved discoverability.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled search initiative” duplicates the Recent Projects section; keep this bullet brief unless you remove or shorten the footer project.
- “Governance/workflows/analytics” repeats NACo themes; frame this as consulting-led transformation, not ongoing channel management.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It should be tightened to foreground enterprise ownership and outcomes, while avoiding overlap with the earlier NACo roles on newsletters, video, and day-to-day channel management.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper summary: “Directed NACo’s enterprise digital communications function, leading web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Recast bullets around biggest outcomes: website migration, analytics stack, studio build, and governance/operating model.
- Add measurable results where possible: site performance gains, publishing efficiency, email growth/engagement, video output, cost savings from in-house production, reporting adoption.
- Example phrasing: “Led redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page Drupal website, supporting 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role; keep this entry at the strategic/enterprise level.
- Video and newsletter management also appear in earlier NACo roles; emphasize scaling, infrastructure, and leadership here.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the later Director role and earlier Digital Media Manager role. Make it more distinct by emphasizing execution leadership, channel ownership, and systems/process improvements rather than broad digital oversight.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a tighter scope statement: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications across web, email, social and video, coordinating editorial and advocacy content across teams.”
- Replace “helping” language with direct ownership: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Sharpen impact where possible: add metrics such as email open/click rates, video cadence/views, stakeholder growth, or workflow time saved.
- Combine the last two bullets into one stronger line: “Built cross-team editorial planning and publishing workflows that improved coordination, consistency and on-time delivery across communications, advocacy and program teams.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update” overlaps with the footer project and 2015–2018 role; keep this only if you can add distinct scale/results.
- Avoid “led digital communications operations” phrasing that duplicates the broader leadership already covered in the Director role.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this skills block overlaps heavily with the header and Core Competencies. It should be tighter, more distinctive, and framed around senior leadership strengths rather than generic communications language.

Suggested edit:
- Replace broad phrases with sharper, executive-level wording:
- Enterprise digital strategy & transformation
- Editorial governance & content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector, membership & advocacy communications
- Audience strategy, messaging & content planning
- Consider reducing to 4 lines to improve scannability and avoid repeating adjacent sections.
- Use parallel noun phrases throughout; avoid mixing “leadership,” “messaging,” and “planning” styles inconsistently.
- If space allows, make one item outcome-oriented, e.g. “Enterprise digital strategy for high-volume public-sector platforms.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy,” “editorial systems and governance,” and “multi-channel communications” substantially duplicate the header and Core Competencies.
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” overlaps with multiple NACo experience bullets; keep this section broader and more category-based.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it reads like a raw tool list and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. In Topline Skills, this should emphasize current, higher-value capabilities and group tools under outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from platform list to capability-led phrasing, e.g.: “Drupal and CMS modernization • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery) • API integrations and workflow automation • Airtable-based operational systems • AI-enabled search experiences”
- Prioritize recent/relevant strengths: lead with Drupal, CMS modernization, AI-enabled search, integrations, and automation; move older/lower-signal platforms later or remove.
- Consider dropping one or two lower-priority items here (e.g. SharePoint, Power Pages) unless they are important for target roles.
- If space allows, sharpen wording: “Airtable systems” → “Airtable-based workflow systems”; “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” → “Web Platforms, Integrations & Automation”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item duplicates the detailed tool inventory in “Technical + IT”; keep Topline Skills broader and more strategic.
- “AI-enabled search experiences” already appears in Core Competencies and the header summary.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster for a senior digital leader, but it reads as a tool list rather than a value statement. It also overlaps heavily with “Data, Analytics & Optimization” in Technical + IT, so this section should emphasize strategic application over software names.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-only to capability-led phrasing, e.g.: “Analytics strategy • KPI framework design • Executive dashboarding • Leadership reporting • User behavior analysis • SEO and performance optimization • GA4, Clarity, Looker Studio, Power BI, BigQuery”
- Put strategic outcomes first and tools last to better match seniority and recent Director/Consultant experience.
- Replace “KPI design” with “KPI framework design” and “Leadership reporting” with “Executive dashboarding and leadership reporting” for stronger, more specific phrasing.
- If space allows, add one impact cue tied to recent work elsewhere on the CV, such as “analytics infrastructure” or “decision-support reporting.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates the “Technical + IT > Data, Analytics & Optimization” section almost exactly.
- Avoid repeating the same five tools here and there unless one section is repositioned as strategic capabilities.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid skill cluster, but it’s too generic and overlaps with both Core Competencies and Technical + IT. Tighten it to emphasize higher-value production leadership and event delivery rather than listing basic capabilities.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe for scope and seniority: “Broadcast-quality video production • Livestream and hybrid event delivery • PTZ camera and studio systems • Virtual event operations”
- Replace “Video production and editing” with a more senior phrase like “Broadcast-quality video production” or “End-to-end video production” to better match the NACo studio build.
- Consider dropping “editing” and “studio operations” if space is tight; those are implied and less differentiating than livestream/hybrid delivery.
- If you want more impact, align wording to recent experience: “In-house studio production” or “Advocacy and event video production.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Multimedia production and livestream operations” already appears in Core Competencies; avoid near-identical phrasing here.
- Tool-level detail is already covered under Technical + IT (“Premiere Pro,” “Livestream studio workflows,” “Podcast production”).

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it’s too bare and duplicates the “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” topline skills section. This item should either be tightened to emphasize strongest/recent platforms or reframed to show level of use.

Suggested edit:
- Prioritize recent, high-value platforms first: **Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- If space allows, add light qualifiers to show depth: **Drupal (enterprise migration, microsites) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- Consider renaming the heading to **CMS & Web Platforms** for cleaner phrasing and consistency with the rest of the CV.
- If you want more impact, replace weaker/less central tools with proficiency framing: **Enterprise CMS: Drupal, WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages; lightweight publishing: GitHub Pages**

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely repeats **Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution**; consider keeping the detailed list here and shortening the topline version.
- Drupal is already strongly evidenced in recent roles, so avoid overexplaining it again elsewhere.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” Tighten it to emphasize implementation tools actually used in recent roles and group items more clearly.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as: “Front-end implementation: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, jQuery”
- Add a second phrase for applied tooling: “Technical delivery: API integrations, Google Tag Manager, Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions”
- If accurate, increase specificity with scope or use case: e.g., “API integrations for CMS/workflow connections” or “GitHub Actions for deployment automation”
- Consider dropping versioned labels (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) unless the rest of the CV uses version-specific naming; “HTML, CSS, JavaScript” is cleaner

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Duplicates “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already listed under Topline Skills; either keep this section more detailed or trim the topline version
- “Workflow automation” appears elsewhere, so avoid adding it here unless tied to a distinct tool or outcome

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow systems leadership. Since “workflow automation” already appears in Core Competencies and Topline Skills, this item should be tighter and more clearly differentiated.

Suggested edit:
- Split by function to show intent, not just tools: “Automation: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier | Work management: Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp | Collaboration: Slack, Microsoft Teams”
- Consider renaming to “Automation, Work Management & Collaboration Tools” for clarity and stronger alignment with your recent systems/governance work.
- Keep only the strongest, most current tools; if space is tight, drop older/redundant PM tools (e.g., Basecamp or Trello) unless used recently.
- If possible elsewhere in the CV, connect these tools to outcomes: e.g., automated reporting, editorial coordination, or cross-team publishing workflows.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable systems” and “Workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills; avoid repeating the same phrasing here.
- Slack/Teams are low-signal unless grouped as collaboration tools rather than featured equally with automation platforms.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful platforms to include, but this item is too bare and undersells a clear strength from recent roles: enterprise email operations and member communications. It should signal scale or use case, not just list tools.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Engagement Platforms**
- Rewrite as: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp — enterprise email campaign delivery, newsletter operations, audience segmentation and member communications**
- If accurate, add one stronger qualifier tied to recent work: **...supporting high-volume newsletters and advocacy/member engagement programs**
- Keep only the most relevant tools; order by recency/enterprise relevance: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp**

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps with work-experience bullets already covering email/newsletter leadership; avoid repeating outcomes here unless you add a distinct capability like **segmentation**, **journey orchestration**, or **campaign operations**.
- “Engagement” is broad; if you keep it, anchor it to email/member communications to stay specific.

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant tool stack, but this item is too generic and overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills.” In a technical section, it should read as a tighter tools/methods list and avoid broad terms that are already covered elsewhere.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with: **GA4 • BigQuery • Power BI • Looker Studio • Microsoft Clarity • Google Search Console • A/B testing • KPI reporting**
- Swap **SEO** for **Google Search Console** or **SEO analysis** to make it more concrete and tool-/method-specific.
- Replace **Dashboarding** with **KPI reporting** or **executive dashboards** for clearer business value.
- Order by strongest/recently evidenced capabilities first: GA4, BigQuery, Power BI, Looker Studio, Clarity.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates **Topline Skills → Analytics, Insights & Optimization**; consider trimming one version or making this section strictly tools while keeping topline focused on outcomes.
- GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery are already named in the 2022–2024 role, so avoid repeating vague terms here.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is too broad and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more foundational and execution-focused, with any concrete scale/results you can add.

Suggested edit
- Reframe around early-career buildout: “Promoted across two digital roles to help launch NACo’s first in-house digital team, improving production workflows across web, email, social and multimedia.”
- Split execution from leadership: “Supported a major website refresh and produced recurring digital content, including livestreams and weekly video updates for member and advocacy communications.”
- Tighten the management line: replace “providing day-to-day guidance” with “mentored a digital media associate” or “coordinated day-to-day work of a digital media associate.”
- Add metrics if available: number of livestreams/videos produced, audience growth, email/social engagement, website traffic impact, or turnaround-time improvements.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; keep this version focused on launching/producing the series, not expanding it.
- “Strengthening workflows” and team-building also appear in later roles; position this as the initial foundation rather than enterprise leadership.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry that shows initiative, especially launching the first podcast. It should be tightened and framed around distinct contributions so it doesn’t overlap too much with later NACo digital/media roles.

Suggested edit
- Lead with the standout achievement: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, scripting, production, and rollout.”
- Make the first sentence more specific and active: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting county-focused programs and policy priorities.”
- Trim generic phrasing like “contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials”; replace with clearer output language such as “produced digital and multimedia content to support program communications.”
- If possible, add scope or outcomes: number of projects supported, podcast episodes launched, audiences reached, or teams/stakeholders coordinated.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Avoid emphasizing broad digital/media leadership here; that is covered more strongly in later NACo roles.
- “Multimedia production” repeats across multiple entries, so keep this item focused on research/program support plus the first-podcast achievement.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid supporting skills list, but it reads more like a mix of software and capabilities. Tightening it into clearer tool categories will make it scan faster and reduce overlap with the stronger “Multimedia Production & Event Delivery” skills section.

Suggested edit:
